consultations.subjectiveNotes: The patient has had a cough and fever for three days. At first, the cough was dry, but now it is productive with yellowish sputum. The fever reaches 38.5 °C, especially in the evening. He also has a headache and feels tired. He has not traveled recently and has had no known contact with COVID-19 cases. He tried acetaminophen, which provided temporary relief.
consultations.objectiveFindings:
Temperature	38.3°C
Respiratory rate	20 breaths/min
SpO₂	97% on room air
Heart rate	92 bpm
Blood pressure	125/78 mmHg
Lung auscultation	Minimal crackles at right base
Sputum	Yellow-green
Appearance	Febrile patient, slightly fatigued
consultations.assessment:
Probable diagnosis: Acute bacterial bronchitis or mild community-acquired pneumonia

Differential diagnosis: Influenza, COVID-19, upper respiratory viral infection

Key points: Productive cough, fever >38°C for 3 days, pulmonary crackles, probable leukocytosis
consultations.plan:
Diagnostic tests:

Complete blood count with differential

CRP (C-reactive protein)

COVID-19 and influenza swab

Chest X-ray (if symptoms worsen)

Medication:

Antibiotic: Amoxicillin 500 mg 3 times/day for 7 days

Antipyretic: Acetaminophen 500-1000 mg every 6-8 hours as needed

Expectorant cough syrup

Adequate hydration and rest

Red flags (return immediately if):

Difficulty breathing

Fever >39°C not responding to medication

SpO₂ <94%

Worsening after 48 hours of antibiotics

Follow-up: Reevaluation in 3 days or sooner if worsening
